title: [US] train_s3: shape, null rates, length distribution
sidecar_rebuild_note: The original sidecar was truncated mid-write and would not parse as JSON. It was regenerated by rebuilding_sidecars.py, which recomputes every numeric field from the profile. The .md deliverable was intact and was not modified.
headline: US slice of train_source3 is 3,170,056 rows (59.9753% of the 5,285,603-row file) and is structurally clean: name_empty=0, prefix_bad=0. Two findings: (1) has_comma (3,059,088) equals rows-addr_empty EXACTLY, so 100% of non-empty US addresses contain a comma; (2) normalize.py:337 gates pin on country=='India' but US dig6/row=0.01335 vs India 0.000194, so the gate admits only 410 India rows while excluding 42,321 US rows.

most_important_number.meaning: US/India per-row dig6 ratio. The country the pin gate ADMITS has 68.9x FEWER six-digit runs per row than the country it EXCLUDES, inverting the gate's apparent intent: 42,321 US rows carry a 6-digit run versus 410 Indian rows.

null_rates_us.assessment: CLEAN. Zero name nulls, zero entity_id prefix violations. The address-null rate is already absorbed by prep.py:23 fill_null("") so it degrades to an empty token list rather than raising.

lengths.note: Two mean-address figures are given because addr_chars counts empty strings as 0 characters (build_profile.py:102-103); both denominators are stated so neither is ambiguous.

name_length_histogram_us.shape: unimodal, right-skewed, hard ceiling. The US top bucket is 80-89 while India's extends to 120, so US names are markedly shorter, consistent with India's compounding multi-word transliterations.

comma_identity.claim: In the US slice has_comma == rows - addr_empty EXACTLY, implying 100% of non-empty US addresses contain at least one comma.
comma_identity.implication: normalize.py:322 splits on ',' and normalize.py:328-335 matches whole components against STATE_MAPS. The uniform US comma structure is the precondition for that exact-match state path to work.
comma_identity.india_off_by_one: Exactly 1 Indian row has content but no comma. Noted as a curiosity, not a defect.

digit_runs_and_pin_gate.code: normalize.py:336-338 captures pin only when len(n)==6 and country=='India'
digit_runs_and_pin_gate.interpretation: run_blocking.py:9 and keys.py:44,58 promote pin into a first-class blocking key, so that key is effectively inert for India (410 rows = 0.0194% of India) and entirely absent for the US in this slice, despite US dig5 (341,738 = 10.7802%/row) indicating US rows are rich in digit runs.
digit_runs_and_pin_gate.caveat: dig5/dig6 count OCCURRENCES (build_profile.py:115-116), not distinct rows, so every per-row figure here is an UPPER BOUND on the distinct-row rate. The conclusion holds either way because the bound is what is used.

statistical_power.verdict: Yes, comfortably large enough to conclude from. Differences of more than a tenth of a percentage point are real.
statistical_power.scope_caveat: This slice cannot speak to France: train_source3 contains only US and India. Any France claim needs the test_s1/2/3 profiles.

already_checked_disposition.REFUTED-1_french_postal_codes: Not re-derived. This train slice contains no France rows at all, so the claim is untestable here and is neither supported nor contradicted.
already_checked_disposition.REFUTED-2_fr_regions_too_thin: Not re-derived. No France rows, so untestable here.

gaps: No per-row flag for 'contains a 5/6-digit number'; dig5/dig6 are occurrence counts, so exact row-level rates are unavailable and all per-row figures are upper bounds.
No state/city/region field: normalize_address outputs are never captured by the profiler.
No true-empty vs whitespace-only distinction: build_profile.py strips before testing emptiness, so '   ' is already counted as empty.
Token counters are top-4000 and pruned of hapax (build_profile.py:45), so no vocabulary size, type-token ratio or unique-business count is derivable.
recommendations: HIGH: revisit the pin gate at normalize.py:336-338. Confining pin to India caps the pin blocking-key population at 410 rows while excluding 42,321 US rows in this slice. Whether extending it improves recall depends on false-positive volume, which this profile cannot measure.
NO CHANGE: address nulls are already handled by prep.py:23 fill_null(""); a 3.5005% address-null rate is a recall ceiling, not a crash risk.

NO CHANGE (advisory): do not truncate ncore early. 99.044% of US names are <=49 chars and 74.5% sit in a single 10-wide bucket, so any character budget for blocking keys would need to sit above ~50 chars. No measurement of the current budget exists, so this is a caution, not a finding.
deliverable_format_note: The two files were the only permitted outputs; this sidecar is the structured half of the P003 work order.
